---
title: "1. Data"
subtitle: "Sources, cleaning decisions and exploratory plots"
---


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
source("R/prepare-data.R")
source("R/plot-theme.R")

lizards <- read_csv("data/lizards-spring-2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(species = factor(species, levels = species_levels))
captures <- read_csv("data/capture-summary.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
analysis <- lizards |> filter(is.na(exclusion))
```
:::


This page goes from the field data to the dataset the model uses.
Every correction and exclusion is listed with its reason, and the plots
show the patterns that motivated the modelling choices on the
[Model page](02-model.qmd).

## Field data

Lizards were captured in three censuses. Only in **spring 2024** were
lizards measured, performance-tested and marked. The **fall 2024**
census (6 months later) recorded only captures. **Spring 2025**
(12 months) is available only as a resighted/not-resighted record for
each marked lizard.


::: {#tbl-captures .cell tbl-cap='Captures per census and species. Fall recaptures count capture events of lizards marked in spring 2024 (some were caught more than once).'}

```{.r .cell-code}
captures |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = season,
    values_from = c(captures, recaptures_of_spring_lizards)
  ) |>
  transmute(
    species,
    `spring 2024 captures` = `captures_spring 2024`,
    `fall 2024 captures` = `captures_fall 2024`,
    `of which recaptures` = `recaptures_of_spring_lizards_fall 2024`
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|species      | spring 2024 captures| fall 2024 captures| of which recaptures|
|:------------|--------------------:|------------------:|-------------------:|
|carolinensis |                   51|                 75|                   5|
|cristatellus |                  626|                678|                 118|
|distichus    |                   16|                  9|                   0|
|equestris    |                   11|                 23|                   8|
|sagrei       |                   57|                 52|                   9|


:::
:::


The analysis uses the three focal species. Two other species were also
marked but cannot support the analysis:

- ***A. distichus*** (16 lizards) had only 2 survivors.
- ***A. equestris*** (11 lizards) has no sprint or bite data. It is also
  far larger (SVL 116--149 mm) than the focal species (about 40--65 mm).

The cleaned dataset, `data/lizards-spring-2024.csv`, has one row for
each of the 734 focal-species lizards marked in spring
2024. It is produced from the raw field data by
`R/process-raw-data.R`.

## Corrections


::: {#tbl-corrections .cell tbl-cap='Corrections applied to individual records. Each is recorded in the `corrections` column of the dataset.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
reasons <- tribble(
  ~correction, ~reason,
  "sex from fall recapture", "Sex at the spring capture disagreed with the fall recapture. Older, larger lizards are easier to sex, so the latest record is used.",
  "implausible date removed", "Recorded in February or March, but the season ran May to June, so almost certainly typos. Dates are not used in the model.",
  "sprint temperature was lizard ID, removed", "The sprint body temperature (714) is the lizard's ID entered in the wrong column.",
  "bite temperature 20.2 corrected to 30.2", "All trials were run near 30 °C, and this lizard's sprint temperature was 30.4 °C.",
  "failed cling trial removed", "Scored 0 on both bark and leaf, so treated as a failed trial on both surfaces.",
  "implausibly short hind toe removed", "Hind toe far shorter than expected for body size (see Morphology below), so set to missing."
)

lizards |>
  filter(!is.na(corrections)) |>
  separate_longer_delim(corrections, "; ") |>
  count(correction = corrections, name = "lizards") |>
  left_join(reasons, by = "correction") |>
  arrange(desc(lizards)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Morphology

Raw linear measurements mostly measure body size. Within each species,
every raw trait correlates strongly with snout--vent length (SVL). We
therefore separate **size**, measured as log SVL, from **shape**,
measured as size-corrected traits. Shape is the log trait minus log
SVL, or minus 2 × log SVL for areas.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
morph_long <- lizards |>
  filter(!exclusion %in% c("no tag", "tag shared by two lizards")) |>
  transmute(
    species, svl,
    `hindlimb (mm)` = hindlimb,
    `head width (mm)` = head_width,
    `hind toe (mm)` = hind_toe_recorded,
    `toepad area (mm²)` = toepad_area,
    flagged = is.na(hind_toe) & !is.na(hind_toe_recorded)
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(species, svl, flagged), names_to = "trait") |>
  mutate(flagged = flagged & trait == "hind toe (mm)") |>
  filter(!is.na(value))

ggplot(morph_long, aes(svl, value, colour = species)) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, !flagged), size = 1.2, alpha = 0.5, stroke = 0) +
  geom_point(data = \(d) filter(d, flagged), shape = 4, size = 2.5, stroke = 0.9, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_wrap(~trait, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_species() +
  labs(x = "SVL (mm)", y = NULL) +
  theme_lizard() +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.5, alpha = 1)))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Morphological traits against SVL (log scales). Traits scale tightly with size, so raw traits mostly re-measure body size. Crosses mark the hind toe lengths set to missing as implausibly short.](01-data_files/figure-html/fig-allometry-1.png){#fig-allometry width=768}
:::
:::



::: {#tbl-size-correlation .cell tbl-cap='Within-species correlation with log SVL, before (raw log trait) and after (size-corrected) size correction.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
analysis |>
  mutate(
    lsvl = log(svl),
    raw_hindlimb = log(hindlimb), rel_hindlimb = log(hindlimb) - lsvl,
    raw_head_width = log(head_width), rel_head_width = log(head_width) - lsvl,
    raw_hind_toe = log(hind_toe), rel_hind_toe = log(hind_toe) - lsvl,
    raw_toepad_area = log(toepad_area), rel_toepad_area = log(toepad_area) - 2 * lsvl
  ) |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(across(starts_with(c("raw_", "rel_")), \(v) cor(v, lsvl))) |>
  pivot_longer(-species, names_to = c("version", "trait"), names_pattern = "^(raw|rel)_(.*)$") |>
  mutate(
    version = if_else(version == "raw", "raw", "size-corrected"),
    trait = str_replace(trait, "_", " ")
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(species), values_from = value) |>
  arrange(trait, version) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|version        |trait       | caro| cris|  sag|
|:--------------|:-----------|----:|----:|----:|
|raw            |head width  | 0.97| 0.99| 0.98|
|size-corrected |head width  | 0.71| 0.52| 0.01|
|raw            |hind toe    | 0.91| 0.96| 0.96|
|size-corrected |hind toe    | 0.15| 0.31| 0.45|
|raw            |hindlimb    | 0.97| 0.99| 0.98|
|size-corrected |hindlimb    | 0.15| 0.50| 0.26|
|raw            |toepad area | 0.91| 0.97| 0.95|
|size-corrected |toepad area | 0.44| 0.69| 0.66|


:::
:::


The predictors used in the model are body size plus one size-corrected
shape trait for each performance trait. Each shape trait was chosen *a
priori* from anole functional morphology:

| Predictor | Definition | Linked performance trait |
|---|---|---|
| size | $\log \text{SVL}$ | all four |
| relative hindlimb | $\log \text{hindlimb} - \log \text{SVL}$ | sprint speed |
| relative head width | $\log \text{head width} - \log \text{SVL}$ | bite force |
| relative hind toe length | $\log \text{hind toe} - \log \text{SVL}$ | clinging on bark (stand-in for claw size) |
| relative toepad area | $\log(\text{fore} + \text{hind toepad area}) - 2 \log \text{SVL}$ | clinging on leaves |

The reasons for these choices:

- **Composite limb lengths.** `forelimb` and `hindlimb` are exact sums of
  their upper and lower segments, so segments and totals cannot be
  included together.
- **Head length is dropped.** In *A. carolinensis* ($n = 47$), relative
  head length correlates strongly with relative head width and with SVL.
  With so few lizards, both head traits could not be separated.
- **Claws.** Clinging to rough bark relies mainly on claws, and clinging
  to smooth leaves on adhesive toepads. Claws were not measured, so
  relative hind toe length stands in for claw size.
- **Toepads.** Fore and hind toepad areas are summed into a single
  total.
- **Implausibly short hind toes.** Twelve hind toe lengths were
  implausibly short, for example 1.0--3.9 mm in lizards of about 43 mm
  SVL whose toes are typically about 7 mm. They are set to missing when
  the robust within-species $z$-score (median and MAD) of log hind toe
  − log SVL is below −5. The values show a clear gap: flagged lizards
  lie between −7.4 and −37, and the next lowest is −4.0.
- **No PCA.** With one or two predictors per performance trait there is
  no dimensionality problem to solve. Principal components would also
  mix size and shape back together, and their loadings, and so their
  meaning, would differ among species.

## Performance

| Trait | Variable | Units / notes |
|---|---|---|
| sprint speed | `sprint` | best trial; cm/s (the raw column name says m/s, but values are cm/s) |
| bite force | `bite` | |
| clinging on bark | `cling_bark` | |
| clinging on leaves | `cling_leaf` | zeros are below the 0.01 resolution |


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
perf_long <- analysis |>
  select(species, sex, sprint, bite, cling_bark, cling_leaf) |>
  pivot_longer(c(sprint, bite, cling_bark, cling_leaf), names_to = "trait") |>
  filter(!is.na(value)) |>
  mutate(
    trait = factor(trait,
      levels = c("sprint", "bite", "cling_bark", "cling_leaf"),
      labels = c("sprint speed (cm/s)", "bite force", "clinging, bark", "clinging, leaf")
    ),
    censored = value == 0,
    value = if_else(censored, leaf_limit / 2, value)
  )

ggplot(perf_long, aes(sex, value, colour = species)) +
  geom_boxplot(data = \(d) filter(d, !censored), outlier.shape = NA, fill = NA, linewidth = 0.4, width = 0.5) +
  geom_point(
    data = \(d) filter(d, !censored),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 1),
    size = 0.9, alpha = 0.4, stroke = 0
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = \(d) filter(d, censored),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.15, height = 0, seed = 1),
    shape = 2, size = 1.5
  ) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  facet_grid(trait ~ species, scales = "free_y", labeller = labeller(species = species_names)) +
  scale_colour_species(guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_lizard() +
  theme(strip.text.x = element_text(face = "bold.italic"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Performance by species and sex (log scale). Triangles at the bottom of the leaf panel are zeros, below the 0.01 resolution, which the model treats as left-censored.](01-data_files/figure-html/fig-performance-1.png){#fig-performance width=768}
:::
:::



::: {#tbl-missing .cell tbl-cap='Missing performance values and leaf-clinging zeros by species. The model estimates both as unknown quantities, so the lizards stay in the analysis.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
analysis |>
  group_by(species) |>
  summarise(
    lizards = n(),
    across(c(sprint, bite, cling_bark, cling_leaf), \(x) sum(is.na(x)), .names = "missing {.col}"),
    `leaf zeros` = sum(cling_leaf_censored, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|species | lizards| missing sprint| missing bite| missing cling_bark| missing cling_leaf| leaf zeros|
|:-------|-------:|--------------:|------------:|------------------:|------------------:|----------:|
|caro    |      47|              1|            1|                  1|                  0|          0|
|cris    |     605|             48|            5|                 15|                 13|         20|
|sag     |      56|              7|            0|                  0|                  0|          2|


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
leaf <- analysis$cling_leaf[!is.na(analysis$cling_leaf)]
skew <- function(v) mean((v - mean(v))^3) / sd(v)^3
sprint_z <- analysis |>
  filter(!is.na(sprint)) |>
  group_by(species, sex) |>
  mutate(z = (log(sprint) - mean(log(sprint))) / sd(log(sprint))) |>
  ungroup()
```
:::


Some features of these distributions shape the model:

- **Leaf-clinging zeros.** 22 lizards scored 0 on
  leaves. The smallest non-zero value is 0.01, the resolution of the
  instrument, so a zero means "below 0.01" rather than no clinging at
  all. The model treats these values as left-censored, estimating each
  somewhere below the limit.
- **Why not log(x + 1).** The common alternative of adding a constant
  before taking logs does not work here. For values this small,
  log(x + 1) is nearly the raw value (correlation
  0.996), and the skew barely changes:
  4.4 raw and 3.5
  after the transform, compared with 0.8
  for log of the non-zero values. Results would also depend on the
  arbitrary constant.
- **Sprint speed has a heavy lower tail.**
  8 lizards are more than 3 SD below their
  species × sex mean, down to 9.7 cm/s.
  These are probably trials where the lizard did not run properly. The
  model currently uses normal residuals; heavier-tailed (Student-t)
  residuals are a possible extension.
- **Sprint speed is coarsely measured.** There are only
  29 distinct sprint values,
  consistent with a fixed track length timed in coarse steps. Near
  150 cm/s this is about ±10% rounding.

## Body temperature at the trial

Body temperature was recorded at the sprint and bite trials, but not at
the clinging trials.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
temp_long <- bind_rows(
  analysis |> transmute(species, sex, trait = "Sprint speed", tb = tb_sprint, perf = sprint),
  analysis |> transmute(species, sex, trait = "Bite force", tb = tb_bite, perf = bite)
) |>
  filter(!is.na(tb), !is.na(perf)) |>
  group_by(trait, species, sex) |>
  mutate(z = (log(perf) - mean(log(perf))) / sd(log(perf))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(trait = factor(trait, c("Sprint speed", "Bite force")))

ggplot(temp_long, aes(tb, z, colour = species)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#d9d8d4", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_point(
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.04, height = 0, seed = 1),
    size = 1.4, alpha = 0.55, stroke = 0
  ) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = FALSE, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~trait, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_colour_species() +
  labs(x = "Body temperature at trial (°C)", y = "Standardised log performance (SD)") +
  theme_lizard() +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2.5, alpha = 1, linewidth = 0)))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![Log performance, standardised within species × sex to remove mean differences, against body temperature at the trial. Lines are linear fits per species. Points are jittered ±0.04 °C because temperatures were recorded to 0.1 °C.](01-data_files/figure-html/fig-temperature-1.png){#fig-temperature width=768}
:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
temp_slopes <- temp_long |>
  group_by(trait) |>
  summarise(slope = coef(lm(z ~ tb))[2])

# curvature on the standardised temperature scale used by the model
temp_curvature <- temp_long |>
  group_by(trait, species) |>
  mutate(w = (tb - mean(tb)) / sd(tb)) |>
  group_by(trait) |>
  group_modify(\(d, k) {
    fit <- summary(lm(z ~ species * w + I(w^2), data = d))$coefficients["I(w^2)", ]
    tibble(curvature = fit[1], se = fit[2])
  })
curv <- \(trait, col) round(temp_curvature[[col]][temp_curvature$trait == trait], 2)
```
:::


Within species and sex, sprint speed increases with temperature (pooled
slope 0.15
SD per °C). Bite force increases clearly only in *A. carolinensis*.

Temperature therefore enters the model as a predictor of sprint and
bite. Performance is expected to follow a thermal performance curve
(TPC), which rises to an optimum and then falls steeply. The trials
cover only a few degrees, probably below the optimum for these species,
so the optimum and critical limits of a full TPC cannot be estimated.
The model instead uses a quadratic in temperature, the local
approximation to a TPC within the observed range. The quadratic is
constrained to be concave, so performance can level off or decline at
the edges of the range but never rise at both ends.

Unconstrained, the curvature in the data is small and slightly
positive. On the standardised temperature scale, the quadratic term is
0.02 ± 0.03
SE for sprint and 0.07 ±
0.03 SE for bite. In *A. sagrei* an
unconstrained quadratic even rises at both the coolest and the warmest
temperatures. With few lizards at the edges of the range, this U-shape
is not a credible thermal response, which is why the model imposes
concavity (see [2. Model](02-model.qmd)).

## Survival and resighting

Each lizard has a resighting history: whether it was seen in fall 2024
($y_2$) and whether it was seen in spring 2025 ($y_3$). The recorded
"6-month survival" is 1 if the lizard was seen at either census. It
therefore counts a lizard that was alive but never seen again as dead.


::: {#tbl-histories .cell tbl-cap='Resighting histories ($y_2 y_3$: 1 = seen) and the naive fall miss rate among lizards known to be alive in fall because they were seen in spring 2025.'}

```{.r .cell-code}
analysis |>
  mutate(history = paste0(seen_fall, surv_12m)) |>
  count(species, history) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = history, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(
    `naive 6-month survival` = sprintf("%.2f", (`01` + `10` + `11`) / (`00` + `01` + `10` + `11`)),
    `fall miss rate` = sprintf("%d/%d = %.2f", `01`, `01` + `11`, `01` / (`01` + `11`))
  ) |>
  select(species, `00`, `01`, `10`, `11`, `naive 6-month survival`, `fall miss rate`) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|species |  00| 01| 10| 11|naive 6-month survival |fall miss rate |
|:-------|---:|--:|--:|--:|:----------------------|:--------------|
|caro    |  38|  5|  0|  4|0.19                   |5/9 = 0.56     |
|cris    | 481| 12| 70| 42|0.20                   |12/54 = 0.22   |
|sag     |  47|  1|  6|  2|0.16                   |1/3 = 0.33     |


:::
:::


Live lizards are often missed in fall, and *A. carolinensis* is missed
more often than it is seen. Species differences in naive survival
therefore partly reflect how easy each species is to find. The model
estimates fall detection jointly with survival, using lizards seen in
spring 2025 but missed in fall.

## The analysis dataset

`prepare_data()` in `R/prepare-data.R` converts the cleaned data into
the form the model uses. It log-transforms and standardises traits
within species, standardises trial temperatures, and marks missing and
censored performance values.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
design <- prepare_data(lizards)
tibble(
  quantity = c("lizards", "species", "performance traits", "morphological predictors",
               "observed performance values", "censored leaf values",
               "seen in fall 2024", "seen in spring 2025"),
  value = c(design$N, design$S, design$J, design$K, sum(design$obs) - sum(design$cens),
            sum(design$cens), sum(design$y2), sum(design$y3))
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|quantity                    | value|
|:---------------------------|-----:|
|lizards                     |   708|
|species                     |     3|
|performance traits          |     4|
|morphological predictors    |     5|
|observed performance values |  2719|
|censored leaf values        |    22|
|seen in fall 2024           |   124|
|seen in spring 2025         |    66|


:::
:::
